suggestions.rationale: Chronic physical illness and functional limitations can be associated with mood symptoms, but an individual secondary relationship requires clinical assessment and case-specific evidence.
evidenceGaps: Mental health evaluation distinguishing secondary emotional impact
Medical nexus opinion addressing causation or aggravation

sourceReferences.note: Legal framework for secondary service connection; does not establish an individual mental-health nexus.

suggestions.rationale: NSAID exposure has been associated with GERD symptoms in observational studies; an individual medication-related theory requires documented exposure, timing, diagnosis, and medical evidence addressing causation or aggravation.
evidenceGaps: Prescription history documenting NSAID or other relevant medication exposure
Medical nexus opinion addressing medication-related causation or aggravation

sourceReferences.citation: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug use as a risk factor for gastro-oesophageal reflux disease: an observational study
sourceReferences.note: Observational evidence found GERD symptoms were more common among NSAID users; this supports an association, not automatic individual causation.

sourceReferences.citation: Global prevalence of, and risk factors for, gastro-oesophageal reflux symptoms: a meta-analysis
sourceReferences.note: Meta-analysis found modestly higher reflux-symptom prevalence among NSAID/aspirin users; this remains population-level evidence.
Legal framework for secondary service connection; does not establish the underlying medical relationship.
